msContents.summary: [p]A collection of recipes for medicinal waters and other remedies, in Latin and Langue d'Oc, on paper, France, mid 15th century.[/p] [p][b]Contents[/b][/p] [p][b]1.[/b] f. 1r: Recipes for medicinal waters for fractures and wounds, in Latin.[/p] [p]f. 1r: Incipit: Ad extrahendum ossa fracta a vulnere. Recype herbam que dicitur mater silve ...; Explicit: Ad sanandum vulnus … et da de dicta aqua in potu.[/p] [p][b]2.[/b] ff. 1v-10r: Recipes for medicinal waters from plants, in Latin, preceded by an index.[/p] [p]The collection is similar to a French one entitled [i]Eaux artificielles avec leurs vertus et propriétés[/i], first printed at Vienne by Pierre Bouttellier (Schenck) about 1484 [ISTC ie00000200; GW 9165], and in several other 15th-century editions. There is also a section (ff. 240-245) in the French edition of the [i]De proprietatibus rerum[/i] printed at Lyons by [Claude Davost], for Jean Genin le Dyamantier, in 1500 [1501?] [ISTC ib00149000; GW 3422], which seems to correspond with the present collection.[/p] [p]f. 1v: Index: Sequitur Rubrica aquarum sequentium. / Primo aqua aurea … Capilli veneris.[/p] [p]f. 2r: Incipit: Sequntur [sic] plures aque et modus quomodo debent fieri. / Et primo aqua aurea sit hoc modo / Recype duas vel tres petras auri ...[/p] [p]f. 10r, line 9: Explicit: … Aqua capilli veneris … collericis / Expliciunt plures aque artifficiales [sic] et ad quid valent.[/p] [p][b]3.[/b] ff. 10r-20r: Recipes for medicinal waters, including descriptions of the medicinal properties of Juniper (ff. 16v-17v) and of an [i]Aqua ardentis[/i] (ff. 18r-20r), in Latin.[/p] [p]The recipes on ff. 10r-13v seem to resemble the first eight recipes listed by Thorndike in his list of 'Vatican Latin MSS. in the history of science and medicine', see [i]Isis[/i], 13 (1929-1930), p. 91, n. 14: Aqua pro oculis … Aqua saliue.[/p] [p]f. 10r, line 10: Incipit: Aqua pro occulis [sic] et l. t. rutam contentus …[/p] [p]f. 20r, line 11: Explicit: ... retinet saporem et odorem.[/p] [p][b]4.[/b] ff. 20r-25v: Recipes for waters and other remedies, some by notable individuals (unidentified), including recipes against verrucas and trembling hands, in Latin.[/p] [p]f. 20r, line 12: Recipe by the Bishop of Béziers, in Latin. Incipit: Hec est Recepta Reuerendi patris domini Episcopi Bitterrensis que est omnium Iuvamentorum pro vero / Recipe pulveris dyamargariton …[/p] [p]f. 20v: Incipit: Recepta de verruchia / Recipe sticadoe arabici ....[/p] [p]f. 23r, lines 13-15: Note: … Presens scriptura Inventa fuit in archa domini mauricii quondam Archiepiscopi Narbonensis.[/p] [p]f. 25r, lines 14-15: Electuary by Magister B. Cabhadelli, Incipit: Electuarium preciosissimum Magistri B. Cabhadelli / Recipe limaturam auri …[/p] [p]f. 25v: Explicit: … Contra gravellam …[/p] [p][b]5.[/b] ff. 26r-27v: Roger Vachon, OF, [i]Las proprietats de la mellissa dutrament ponsirada[/i], a treatise on the properties of the Melissa officinalis, i.e. lemon balm, in Langue d'Oc.[/p] [p]For Roger Vachon, see E. Wickersheimer, [i]Dictionnaire biographique des médecins en France au moyen âge[/i] (Paris: Droz, 1936), p. 722.[/p] [p]The treatise is similar to the entry on the 'Eaue de melice' in the French collection entitled [i]Eaux artificielles avec leurs vertus et propriétés[/i], first printed at Vienne in about 1484 (see above no. 2), as noted by Wickersheimer.[/p] [p]f. 26r: Incipit: Siegon si las proprietats de la mellissa dutrament ponsirada et cetera / pernnerament da questa Erba …[/p] [p]f. 27v: Explicit: … et en bonn memoria / [Underlined in red] A questa perfiecha determinacion es estada bayllada per i. maystre Reuerent moyne. ffrayre Rogier [Vachon] excellent maystre en medicina Suss las proprietats de la mellissa, dutrament appellada ponsirada.[/p] [p][b]6.[/b] ff. 28r-30v: Twenty-nine recipes for medicinal waters, in Langue d'Oc.[/p] [p]f. 28r: Incipit: Ayga de flor de lis blanc es bona per far lo visage blanc …[/p] [p]f. 30v, lines 9-10: Explicit: … Ayga composta mereuilhosa per los huelhs ... Car sapias que aysse es ayga / mot cordial.[/p] [p][b]7.[/b] ff. 30v-31v: Seven recipes (against freckles, for the eyes, and a laxative) and a description of the healing properties of gentian, in Latin.[/p] [p]f. 30v, line 11: Incipit: Ad Restringendum lentigines faciey [sic] Recipe semen malue …[/p] [p]f. 31v: Explicit: … Virtutes seu proprietates / herbe gensiane ... omni corpori qui ea vsus / fuerit mirabiliter dat Sanitatem.[/p]

msItem.title: [p]A collection of recipes for medicinal waters and other remedies, in Latin and Langue d'Oc (Provençal)[/p]

objectDesc.supportDesc: 1 volume[p]On paper; watermark: bull's head, with eyes and nostrils (height: c. 38 mm; width: c. 25 mm; distance between chain-lines: 38 mm): similar to Briquet nos 14970 (height: 42 mm; width: 27 mm; distance between chain-lines: 38 mm; Toulouse 1454-1458, Aix-en-Provence 1457, Fribourg 1458, Marburg 1461) and 14975 (height: 40 mm; width: 32 mm; distance between chain-lines: 35 mm; Sion 1475).[/p] [p]31 leaves of originally 32 (wanting first leaf); old foliation '116-[146]' in brown ink in upper margin, faint; modern foliation '1-31' in pencil. 204 x 140 mm; written area 150/171 x 90/100 mm, in single column, 26-36 written lines to a page; no ruling.[/p] [p]Collation: 1[sup]18-1[/sup] (wanting i), 2[sup]14[/sup]; without quire signatures or catchwords.[/p] [p]Secundo folio: Sequntur plures.[/p] [p] Written by two hands (ff. 1r-25v and 26r-31v respectively) in a French cursive book-hand ([i]Gothic Batârde[/i]).[/p] [p]Decoration: Four- to six-line initials at the beginning of works, and two-line paragraph-initials throughout, all in black ink. Explicit to Roger Vachon's [i]Las proprietats de la mellissa[/i] underlined in red and with marginal penflourished decoration in blue in the margin (f. 27v).[/p] [p]Marginal annotations (ff. 3r, 9r), nota signs in the form of maniculae ([i]passim[/i]) and a decorated bracket (f. 21r) added in brown ink by the same hand of similar maniculae in MS. 523 ([i]passim[/i]).[/p] [p]Binding: Modern limp parchment binding made of a leaf from a manuscript copy of Henricus de Segusio (c. 1200-1271), [i]Summa super tituli Decretalium[/i], Book II, in Gothic bookhand, with running title, paragraph marks and marginal chapter numbers in alternating red and blue, and marginal notes framed in red, measuring c. 334 x 236 mm, written space c. 305 x 160 mm, in two columns, 56 written lines per column (ruling not visible), Southern France, 14th century.[/p] [p]Upper margin of last leaf damaged, stained throughout.[/p]

history.provenance: [p]The manuscript was formerly bound as last in a composite volume together with MSS 523 [Miscellanea Alchemica XX] and 707 [Rupescissa] (in this order), as suggested by the list of contents at the beginning of the miscellany (f. 1r of MS. 523), and confirmed by the old foliation in a 16th-century hand running consecutive in the upper margin of rectos in all three manuscripts (faint in MS. 707 and the present one).[/p] [p]The manuscripts were separated into three volumes some time in the late 19th or early 20th century, and bound in wrappers made of parchment leaves from different medieval manuscripts.[/p]
